- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.27) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% above recent mean), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3–4% above peak or use 20-day moving average for stabilization.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.77) and price is trending up, model frequently overcorrects; apply downward bias of 1–3% to prevent overbought bias.
- When true outcome shows strong mean reversion (price drops >5% from recent peak), model often fails to adjust; add 1–2% downward correction if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- For 30-day forecasts, if last 3–5 days show downward momentum + negative sentiment, model tends to lag; add 1–3% upward bias to counteract lag.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.80 → 0.27 → 0.80), model often misreads trend direction; use sentiment-weighted average of last 5 days to anchor forecast.
